_formato: Same structure as quiz.json: the FIRST option is correct; the app shuffles them.

g01.p: What process sculpted the pillars of the Lauca River Valley Cathedral?
o: Intense water runoff over the slopes
g01.e: Runoff over layers of lake sediments and volcanic ash has carved the pillars since the Pleistocene.

g01.p: What is the name of the sequence of sediments and ash at this geosite?
g01.e: The Lauca Formation is 6.2 to 2.6 million years old (Late Miocene–Late Pliocene).

g01.p: What color are the interbedded volcanic ash layers?
g01.e: The volcanic ash is whitish and contrasts with the brown lake sediments.

g02.p: What are the oval-shaped lavas seen at the Morro de Arica called?
g02.e: They form when lava cools rapidly on contact with seawater.

g02.p: What period do the rocks of the Morro de Arica belong to?
g02.e: Their fossils date them to the Middle Jurassic, 170 to 163 million years ago.

g02.p: What do the fossil bivalves, ammonites and corals of the Morro indicate?
o: The rocks formed in a shallow sea
There was a large freshwater lake
g02.e: They are marine organisms of shallow environments.

g03.p: Which mineral gives the Amuyo crusts their yellowish-green color?
g03.e: Orpiment gives yellowish-green tones; realgar gives orange-red ones.

g03.p: What are the heat-tolerant bacteria in these lagoons called?
g03.e: Thermophilic bacteria build structures called stromatolites and thrombolites.

g03.p: Why is this geosite important for studying the origin of life?
o: Similar organisms have existed on Earth for about 3,500 million years
A meteorite with life fell here
It is the coldest lagoon in the world
g03.e: Its bacterial colonies help us understand early life and the possibility of life elsewhere.

g04.p: Why is the Cerro Dragón dune classified as fossil or relict?
o: It no longer has an active source of sand
g04.e: Without a beach to feed it, the dune receives no new sand.

o: During the Last Glacial Maximum, about 20,000 years ago
g04.e: Sea level was about 100 m lower and exposed a sandy platform.

g04.p: What threatens the integrity of the dune?
o: Urban growth, sand extraction and recreational activities
g04.e: Real-estate pressure in Iquique has fragmented it.

g05.p: Why is the Pintados salt flat fossil or inactive?
o: It receives no recharge from surface streams
It froze thousands of years ago
g05.e: Its salt crust is disconnected from deep groundwater.

g05.p: About how many figures make up the Pintados geoglyphs?
g05.e: About 450 figures over 50,000 m², made by pre-Hispanic peoples between 700 and 1500 AD.

g05.p: What technique was mainly used to make the geoglyphs?
g05.e: Removing surface material creates contrast with the natural ground.

o: A lagoon or place where water springs up
g06.e: Puquios are lagoons where groundwater emerges.

g06.p: Which microbial communities live in the Llamara puquios?
g06.e: Both are made of gypsum and microorganisms in extreme conditions.

g06.p: Why do these lagoons have such high evaporation?
o: The extreme solar radiation of the Atacama Desert
They sit high on a volcano
g06.e: The Atacama Desert receives the highest solar radiation on the planet.

g07.p: Where does El Tatio rank among the world's geothermal fields?
g07.e: It is the most important in Chile and Latin America and the third in the world.

g07.p: What share of the world's geysers is at El Tatio?
g07.e: Its geysers make up 8% of these features worldwide.

g07.p: What temperature do the fluids reach at depth?
g07.e: They reach 280 °C at depth and 86 °C at the surface.

g08.p: Why did the arches of La Portada form?
o: The sedimentary rocks resist waves less than the volcanic rocks at the base
They were carved by ancient peoples
g08.e: Differential erosion wears away the La Portada Formation's sedimentary rocks faster.

g08.p: What rocks are seen at the base of the cliff and arches?
o: Volcanic rocks of the La Negra Formation (Jurassic)
g08.e: The La Negra Formation formed from volcanic activity 180 to 143 million years ago.

g08.p: Why is access to the beach restricted?
o: Risk of rockfall from the cliff
g08.e: The cliff keeps retreating slowly and steadily.

g09.p: What makes Monturaqui crater unique in Chile?
o: It is the only confirmed meteorite impact structure in the country
It is the deepest crater in the world
g09.e: It was discovered in 1962 from aerial photographs.

g09.p: How long ago did the meteorite strike?
g09.e: It happened in the Middle Pleistocene.

g09.p: What type of meteorite was it?
g09.e: Its remains, along with the impactites, have been removed by unregulated expeditions.

g10.p: What are the spheres that give this rock its spotted look called?
g10.e: They average 6 cm and formed as minerals arranged themselves while the magma crystallized.

g10.p: How many orbicular rocks have been described worldwide?
g10.e: They are rare, which is why this one became a Nature Sanctuary in 1981.

g10.p: Which intrusive body does the orbicular tonalite belong to?
g10.e: The Relincho Pluton is 195 to 180 million years old (Early Jurassic).

g11.p: What are the layers rich in vertebrate fossils at Los Dedos called?
g11.e: They belong to the Mina Fosforita sub-unit, about 7 million years old.

g11.p: Which giant shark left teeth over 15 cm long here?
g11.e: Its teeth stand out for their size.

g11.p: How many fossil vertebrate species have been identified?
g11.e: They include sharks, crocodiles, penguins, whales, marine sloths and more.

g12.p: What rocks form the orange layers of Quebrada Pinte?
g12.e: They belong to the fossil-rich Lautaro Formation.

g12.p: What covered this area 190 to 170 million years ago?
g12.e: In the Early to Middle Jurassic much of southern South America was under the sea.

g12.p: Where can you see collections of its fossils?
g12.e: The museum is inside the ravine.

g13.p: Which dinosaur was found at Pichasca?
g13.e: Antarctosaurus wichmannianus, from the Late Cretaceous.

g13.p: What forms the roof of Casa de Piedra?
o: A sill, a more resistant intrusive rock
g13.e: The softer sedimentary rocks below eroded faster, leaving the overhang.

g13.p: Which culture lived in the rock shelter about 9,000 years ago?
g13.e: They left arrowheads, rock paintings and basketry.

g14.p: What are terraces formed by wave erosion called?
g14.e: They record sea-level changes and the uplift of the Coastal Range.

g14.p: What allows a southern forest to exist at Fray Jorge?
g14.e: Olivillo and canelo trees survive thanks to the camanchaca.

g14.p: How old is the youngest terrace (T5)?
g14.e: It lies at 10 m a.s.l.; T2 is 321,000 and T4 is 122,000 years old.

g15.p: What human find stands out near Quebrada Quereo?
o: Remains of the oldest dated human in South America

g15.p: What extinct fauna is preserved under the dunes?
g15.e: They are between 8,000 and 30,000 years old.

g15.p: Why are some Quereo dunes still active?
o: Wind carries sand from the beaches
g15.e: The wind keeps bringing sand from the beach.

g16.e: Rano Kao, Poike and Terevaka volcanoes form the island's volcanic complex.

g16.p: What does the Rano Kao crater hold?
g16.e: It is one of the island's key freshwater reserves and an archive of past climates.

g16.p: Which ceremonial village sits on the crater's slope?
g16.e: Orongo is of great significance to Rapa Nui culture.

g17.p: What is the Devil's Staircase geologically?
o: A dike: intrusive rock that cut vertically through other rocks
g17.e: Magma rose through fractures and solidified quickly.

g17.p: Why does the dike stand out above the ground?
o: It is more resistant to erosion than the surrounding rock
g17.e: Its fractures control how blocks break off, forming the 'steps'.

g17.p: Which project seeks to conserve this geosite?
g17.e: It seeks to conserve and showcase it for local communities.

g18.p: Which aquatic sloth lived at Quirilluca?
g18.e: It lived 3 to 2 million years ago, at the end of the Pliocene.

g18.p: What are the flat surfaces above the cliff?
g18.e: They formed underwater by wave abrasion and were later uplifted.

g18.p: What are the two 5 m blocks on the beach?
o: Remains of a collapsed rock arch

g19.p: Why are the Concón Dunes fossil dunes?
o: A cliff cuts them off from beach sand
g19.e: They sit on a marine terrace at 80 m a.s.l.

g19.p: When did these wind-blown sands accumulate?
g19.e: They cover marine sediments of the Caleta Horcón Formation (Late Pliocene).
Its location in the largest coastal urban area makes it very fragile.

g20.p: What is Cerro Santa Lucía called in the Mapuche language?
g20.e: It was declared a Historic Monument in 1983.

g20.p: What shape do the most distinctive columns have?
g20.e: Columns can have 3 to 6 sides; hexagonal ones are the most distinctive.

g20.p: What do the rocks of Santa Lucía, San Cristóbal and Manquehue represent?
o: Magmatic roots of early Miocene volcanoes
g20.e: They are 22 to 20 million years old.

g21.p: Why are the Lo Valdés 'plates' vertical?
o: Deformation during the rise of the Andes tilted them
They were always deposited that way
g21.e: They were originally horizontal layers on the seafloor.

g21.p: How many ammonite species have been found?
g21.e: Ammonites are extinct shelled cephalopods, relatives of the nautilus.

g21.p: How deep was the sea where these layers formed?
g21.e: They formed 152 to 129 million years ago on volcanic rocks.

g22.p: What gives the ravine's rocks their yellow-orange color?
o: Hot fluids from San José volcano altered the minerals
g22.e: They produced clays and iron oxides.

g22.p: Which geological hazard occurs in the ravine during heavy rain?
g22.e: The altered rocks are brittle and erode easily.

g22.p: What can a large debris flow here affect?
g22.e: It can damage the water intake on the Maipo River.

o: A pyroclastic flow deposit from a huge eruption
g23.e: It is linked to the collapse of an eruption column kilometers high.

g23.p: Which volcanic depression formed in that eruption?
g23.e: Today Laguna del Diamante, in Argentina, fills it.

g23.p: What makes up 85 to 90% of the deposit at Machalí?
g23.e: It contains very few rock fragments and some pumice.

g24.p: How many kinds of dinosaurs left tracks at Termas del Flaco?
g24.e: Some may belong to the ichnogenus Brontopodus.

o: Ash from volcanic eruptions that buried them
g24.e: The ash covered the footprints soon after they formed.

o: Along a coastal lagoon near a coral reef
g24.e: The climate was tropical to subtropical.

g25.p: What type of fault is the El Fierro Fault?
g25.e: It verges east and is associated with an anticline.

g25.p: What recent event was linked to this fault?
g25.e: It shows the fault has been active since the Late Eocene.

g25.p: Which basin did these faults control from about 37 million years ago?
g25.e: They controlled its eastern edge since the end of the Eocene.

g26.p: What rock forms the Piedra de la Iglesia in Constitución?
g26.e: It crystallized in the Late Triassic, about 224 million years ago.

o: Remains of an ancient cliff eroded by the sea
g26.e: The cliff formed in the Late Pleistocene.

g26.p: What extra value do the Constitución Rocks have?
g26.e: Gulls, boobies, cormorants and pelicans nest there.

g27.p: How did the 'cups' of the Claro River form?
o: Erosion by rock fragments dragged along the riverbed
g27.e: Erosion progressively deepened pools in the lava.

g27.p: What rocks does the river flow over at Siete Tazas?
g27.e: They belong to the Planicies y Valles Volcanic Unit (Pliocene–Pleistocene).

g27.p: According to the text, what do columnar joint fractures resemble?

g28.p: Why is the geosite called 'La Cárcel' (The Prison)?
o: Its vertical columns look like the bars of a cell
It is hard to leave the valley
g28.e: The columns are up to 20 m high.

g28.p: Which volcanic complex do these rocks belong to?
g28.e: They are about 116,000 years old (Late Pleistocene).

g28.p: Which sport makes this place famous?
g28.e: It is one of the most attractive climbing spots in South America.

g29.p: What did the Los Pincheira lavas flow beneath?
g29.e: They advanced gradually because they had to melt the ice.

g29.p: About how far did these lavas travel?
g29.e: They are among the longest lava flows in southern Chile.

g29.p: Who used the cave as a hideout?

g30.p: What are rock fragments picked up by magma called?
g30.e: They come from rocks of the Metamorphic Basement.

g30.p: Which very special rock formed through magma interaction?
g30.e: Only two are documented in Chile and about 30 worldwide.

g30.p: How long ago did the Cobquecura magmas interact?
o: About 210 million years ago (end of the Triassic)
g30.e: It happened deep in the Earth's crust.

g31.p: Where does the name 'Los Pangues' come from?
o: The abundant pangue or nalca plants
g31.e: Their leaves can exceed a meter across.

g31.p: Which layer forms the roof of the grotto?
o: A more resistant layer with lithic bombs
g31.e: The weaker layers below eroded, forming the cavity.

g31.p: How long ago did the eruptions that formed these layers occur?
g31.e: They were large explosive eruptions of Nevados de Chillán in the Holocene.

g32.p: Which marine reptile stands out at Caleta Cocholgüe?
g32.e: It is the youngest plesiosaur described to date.

g32.p: Which great transition in geological time do these rocks record?
o: From the Mesozoic to the Cenozoic era, 66 million years ago
g32.e: It shows in the change of fossil fauna between the Quiriquina and Curanilahue formations.

o: Fossil structures made by organisms in sediments
g32.e: They are also called trace fossils.

g33.p: What shape does an anticline have?
g33.e: A concave fold ('U') is called a syncline.

g33.p: What does it mean that the fold is 'overturned'?
o: Its axial plane is tilted and one limb is inverted
g33.e: On the overturned limb, older layers lie above younger ones.

o: A deep fault pushing the layers from below
g33.e: It happened between 14 and 9 million years ago.

g34.p: What rock forms the Piedra del Águila viewpoint?
g34.e: It belongs to the Southern Coastal Batholith (Late Paleozoic).

g34.p: At what depth did the batholith magmas cool?
Which metamorphic rock is found around the viewpoint?
g34.e: It formed when sedimentary rocks were heated above 600 °C.

g35.p: When did the eruption that built the Navidad cone begin?
g35.e: Hence its name: it began on Christmas (Navidad).

g35.p: Why did so much livestock die?
How long did lava flow down the Lolco River valley?
g35.e: It reached 10 km from its source.

g36.p: How many layers can be seen in the canyon wall?
g36.e: They record ash falls, pyroclastic flows and lahars.

g36.p: Which deposit lies at the base of the sequence?
g36.e: It is Llaima's largest and oldest eruption.

g36.p: Where does Llaima rank in the specific-risk ranking?
g36.e: It is one of Chile's most active volcanoes.

g37.e: It is the Mapuche name of Villarrica volcano.

g37.p: What does Villarrica's crater have that only 7 volcanoes in the world have?
o: An open crater with a lava lake
g37.e: It is a true natural laboratory.

g37.p: Where does Villarrica rank in the specific-risk ranking?
g37.e: Because of its high hazard and nearby towns, it is monitored in real time.

g38.e: It was used to carve Fuerte Niebla's battery and moat.

g38.p: How many ancient environments are recognized in the cancagua layers?
g38.e: Beach and shallow platform, estuary, and coastal barrier with dunes and a delta.

g38.p: In what year was Fuerte Niebla built?
g38.e: It was declared a Historic Monument in 1950.

g39.p: What is lava with a rough, rope-like surface called?
g39.e: Aa lava, in contrast, has sharp-edged blocks.

g39.p: How long did the 1971 lava take to travel about 16.5 km?
g39.e: Lava flows are among the greatest hazards near volcanoes.

g39.p: How many eruptions has Villarrica had in the last 440 years?
g39.e: Some calm and others very explosive.

g40.p: In what year did the Mirador cone form?
g40.e: A prehistoric scoria cone reactivated between April and May 1979.

g40.p: How many volcanic centers does the Carrán-Los Venados field have?
g40.e: They include scoria cones, craters and maars.

g40.p: What could this volcanic field let scientists study?
o: How a volcano forms from its earliest stages
g40.e: Its high activity makes it scientifically valuable.

g41.p: Which Pilauco find is the oldest of its kind in South America?
g41.e: It would belong to a person of about 72 kg and 1.82 m.
They were part of the Pleistocene megafauna.

g41.p: What hypothesis is proposed for the megafauna extinction?
g41.e: Evidence of an impact has been found in the area.

g42.p: What blocked the ancient Petrohué River valley?
g42.e: The lava flowed while the valley still held ice from the Llanquihue Glaciation.

g42.p: How old are the lavas at Petrohué Falls?
Which marsupials live in the park?
o: Long-nosed shrew opossum and monito del monte
g42.e: The park is part of a biosphere reserve.

g43.p: When did Chaitén volcano's last eruption begin?
g43.e: It came as a surprise because there was no instrument network.

g43.p: What did the Chaitén eruption lead Sernageomin to create?
g43.e: It now monitors the country's most dangerous volcanoes.

g43.p: What partly destroyed the town of Chaitén?
o: Lahars from rain remobilizing the ash
g43.e: They came down the Blanco River valley.

g44.p: What shaped the towers of Cerro Castillo?
g44.e: Erosion according to rock hardness carved its pinnacles.

g44.p: Which intrusive rocks are part of the mountain?
g44.e: It formed about 98 to 93 million years ago.
It is visible from the Carretera Austral.

g45.p: Which mineral mainly makes up the marble of the Marble Chapel?
g45.e: Water dissolves this mineral and has shaped the rocks.

g45.p: For how long has water been shaping these rocks?
g45.e: Since shortly before the start of the Holocene.

g45.p: How do you reach the geosite?
o: By boat on Lake General Carrera
g45.e: It is 5 km from Puerto Río Tranquilo.

g46.p: Why did some parts of the rock resist erosion better?
o: They were hardened by added silica

g46.p: What kind of eruptions produced these rocks?
g46.e: They happened 152 to 142 million years ago (Ibáñez Formation).

g47.p: What are the light rocks of the Cuernos del Paine?
o: Granites intruded about 13 million years ago
g47.e: They contrast with the dark Cretaceous sedimentary rocks.

g47.p: What do the dark rocks of the Cuernos indicate?
o: A deep sea in the Cretaceous
g47.e: They belong to the Punta Barrosa and Cerro Toro formations.

g47.p: What carved the horns, cirques and ridges?
g47.e: Glacial erosion acted according to each rock's hardness.

g48.p: What does 'Pali-Aike' mean in the Aónikenk language?
g48.e: The park is 196 km northeast of Punta Arenas.

g48.p: What shape is the Pali-Aike cone?
o: A horseshoe open to the north
g48.e: A lava flow escaped through the opening.

g48.p: What was found in Pali-Aike Cave?
o: Evidence of human occupation about 9,000 years old
g48.e: It helped reconstruct the history of early inhabitants of southern Patagonia.

g49.p: Which rocks form most of the summits of the Dientes de Navarino?
g49.e: The diorites are about 100 million years old (Late Cretaceous).

g49.p: What shape do glacier-carved valleys have?
Which town is about 6 km from this geosite?
g49.e: It is the southernmost city in the world.
